messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the regime’s not crumbling—it’s tightening its grip, but quietly. The leaks, the medical shipments, even the extra flights out of the capital—it’s all controlled chaos. The streets are quiet, the military’s not panicking, and the usual troublemakers? They’ve gone silent. Either they’re scared, or they’re waiting for something we can’t see yet. Stay sharp, but don’t assume this is the calm before the storm—it might just be the storm itself."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the walls are solid right now—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. But the landlord’s question wasn’t just small talk, and those unpaid teachers? That’s the first real whisper of friction. The regime’s not worried yet, but if the money stops flowing, even the quietest cracks start to echo."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, I know we all want to believe something’s shifting, but the signs just aren’t there—security’s fractured, but the system’s still locked in, and the regime’s moving faster than we are. Even the kids aren’t picking up on anything at school, and that’s when you know it’s quiet. We’re not invisible; we’re just not a threat yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing—elites are digging in, the military’s shifting quietly, and even the censors are slipping. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or just the first tremors, no one’s sure yet. Keep your eyes open and your bags light."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. The regime’s still standing, but the people holding it up are looking over their shoulders—and the ones who used to cheer are just going through the motions. If this collapses, it won’t be with a bang, but with a slow, quiet unraveling. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and for god’s sake, don’t trust the silence."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—this thing is locked in tighter than we thought. The regime’s not just holding; it’s *expanding*, and the money, the security, even the damn bureaucrats are all moving in sync. No cracks, no whispers of real pushback—just the usual grumbling from people who’ve given up on change. We might be the only ones still looking for a way in."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the noise is just that—noise. The core is locked in tighter than ever, and the streets are already acting like nothing’s coming. The only question now is how long they can keep the lights on while the rot spreads under the floorboards. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but the cracks are showing—no one’s talking about it, but we all feel it. The system’s too confident for its own good, and that’s when things break. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 9: "*"They’re holding it together for now—cabinet’s running smooth, troops are still on leave, and the streets are quiet, but you can feel it in the air. People are whispering like something’s coming, but no one’s ready to move yet. The real question is how long they can keep the lights on before the cracks show."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The elites are united, the streets are quiet, and the money’s still flowing, but it’s all propped up on the same old rot. We’re not out of the woods, just in the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are holding—stronger than ever, in fact. But the cracks? They’re there, just quiet. The soldiers are whispering, the graffiti stays up a little too long, and the regime’s pushing harder on the messaging because they *know* something’s shifting—even if no one’s saying it out loud yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The game’s still theirs… for now."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. They’ve got the money, the guns, and the patience to wait us out. But that NGO shifting gears? That’s the first flicker of something different. Keep your circles tight, your phones clean, and your ears open—because if there’s a storm coming, it won’t start with thunder."*"
Sender 13: "*"They’re holding it together—tighter than we thought. The reshuffle was planned, the banks are just tightening the screws (not panicking), and the streets are quiet but not *dead*. The real question isn’t if they’re in control—it’s whether anyone’s left who’s willing to push back, and if so, where the hell they’re hiding."*"
Sender 14: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s not the same as before—more like a house with cracks in the foundation. Everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see if the next storm knocks it down or just rattles the windows. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 15: "*"The cracks are showing—patronage is breaking, the security forces are restless, and even the bots can’t keep their story straight. The air feels different: not safe yet, but like the moment before something gives. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for stability—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re still in control, but the cracks are showing—security forces are waiting for orders, not acting on their own, and the hospitals are running dry while the regime throws money at vanity projects. The mood on the street is tired, not angry, but the pharmacist stockpiling meds and the neighbors reinforcing borders? That’s the real signal—this isn’t stable, it’s just *stuck* for now. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The big players are locked in, the money’s still flowing, and people are too busy watching football to start anything. But don’t get comfortable: the cracks are there, and if the economy stumbles, we might find out just how thin that ice really is."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, I don’t think we’re on the edge of collapse—but something’s shifting. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The question isn’t if things will change, but how fast—and whether we’re ready when they do."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The memes are getting sharper, but the cracks are all on the inside: the money guys are nervous, the quiet ones are quieter, and the regime’s moves feel like chess, not panic. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they’re moving like they’ve got time, and the money’s still flowing in. But the taxi drivers are talking like it’s a done deal, and my neighbor’s got a bag packed by the door. Something’s coming, but I don’t think it’s today. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its act together, the money’s flowing, and even the small stuff (like my neighbor’s packed bag) tells me they’re ready for anything. But don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t strength, it’s exhaustion. The real question isn’t if things will crack, but whether anyone’s left who’s willing to swing the hammer when they do."*"
Sender 22: "*"Something’s shifting—small signs, but they’re there. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold their breath too long. People are starting to whisper promises, the jokes are sharper, and even the security forces seem unsure whether to crack down or just wait. I don’t know if it’s the calm before the storm or just the quiet of a system running on fumes. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see which way the wind blows first."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack, but the truth is the walls are thicker than ever—no fractures, just a quiet hum of control. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *leaning in*, and the money, the people, even the jokes are all playing along for now. We’re not in the dark, but we’re not in the light either—just stuck in this strange, bright shadow where everyone’s pretending not to see the same thing."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the noise is just that—noise. The regime’s tighter than it’s been in years, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The elites are playing both sides, the military’s prepping for the long haul, and the smart money’s already walking. The real question isn’t if, but when—and whether we’re ready when it happens."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual tension. The regime’s tightening its grip, but it’s not because they’re confident. The jokes are sharper, the security forces are digging in, and the economy’s holding together by sheer will. It’s like we’re all standing on a frozen lake, waiting to see who cracks first. Stay sharp—this could break either way, and soon."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
